pages.text:
A refinery column that splits creosote and Crude Oil into fractions with heat. The taller and wider the column, the more it makes, and the faster.
# Building
A solid column 2x2 or 3x3 across and 4 to 16 tall, of casings and Tray Level Casings with one controller. The controller and the trays can't be in the top or bottom layer, and on a 3x3 the controller goes on the outside. The controller's side is the front.
Formed, it becomes a refinery tower: a round shell in flanged tray sections, a sight glass on each tray showing what pools there and the vapour rising, platforms and a caged ladder, draw-off pipes for each product, a condenser bank on top and a fired reboiler at the base that glows when it's hot. You can walk on its platforms.

# Size
It feeds 10 mB/t for a 2x2 four high, more by its cross-section (a 3x3 x2.25) and height (per 4 blocks): 20 mB/t for a 2x2x8, 90 mB/t for a 3x3x16. Its heat buffer grows the same way, and its tanks with its volume.
# Creosote (1,000 mB, 4,000 HU, 350°C)
- 4 high: 250 Naphtha, 2 Pitch.
- 6 high: 250 Naphtha, 450 Heavy Oil, 1 Pitch.
- 8 high and up: 250 Naphtha, 300 Light Oil, 300 Heavy Oil, 1 Pitch.

# Crude Oil (1,000 mB, 5,000 HU, 380°C)
- 6 high: 100 Refinery Gas, 200 Naphtha, 350 Diesel, 250 Bitumen.
- 10 high: also 150 Kerosene and 150 Heavy Oil (100 Refinery Gas, 200 Naphtha, 250 Diesel, 100 Bitumen).
- 14 high and up: more of the light cuts: 130 Refinery Gas, 270 Naphtha, 190 Kerosene, 230 Diesel, 90 Heavy Oil, 60 Bitumen.
Below 6 it's too short for Crude Oil.

# Ports
A new column starts without ports: set a heat port (a Fuel Burner under it heats it), a feed port, and a port for each product you want out, with the Wrench in Port mode. Each product has its own mode, and Refinery Gas leaves by gas conduits.
# Steam stripping
Steam in its steam tank raises the Naphtha of every batch (out of the Heavy Oil for creosote, the Bitumen for Crude Oil): Steam +15%, High-Pressure +30%, Superheated +50%, 100 mB a batch.
# Upgrades
Speed Upgrades feed it 2^(n/2) times as fast, using heat as fast. Heat Upgrades cut the heat per batch to 0.8^n.
